source.title: An efficient algorithm for learning-based visual localization.
source.authors: Jindi Zhong; Zi-Yuan Guo; Hong-Xia Wang; Huan-Shui Zhang

record.file_problem: The full paper is present; some figure text near the end is garbled, but the relevant Table 2 is legible.
record.tranche_reason: Reports optimizer comparisons on visual-localization regression, an additional setting for studying training and validation performance.
record.gate_note: Table 2 reports training loss, validation loss, and minimum validation loss for six optimizers at 50 and 150 iterations. These are localization-regression results, not classification or language results; no random-label memorization, batch-size, width, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example removal tests are reported.
record.test_reason: The study cites original sources but tests none of V1–V8. Its optimizer comparisons measure KITTI coordinate-regression loss, outside V4's image-classification and language benchmarks. Dropout and weight decay are used without testing their effects; Hessian estimation does not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that Diag-OCP accelerates convergence, improves visual-localization generalization performance, and is robust to learning-rate tuning. They leave validation across more datasets and architectures to future work. Their claim of the lowest training loss is contradicted by Table 2, and their reported 57.1% validation-loss reduction versus Adam does not match the listed values.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a lightweight CNN for continuous coordinate regression on KITTI, with weight decay and tuned optimizer parameters; the claim versions concern classification or language generalization, memorization, or related measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer, iteration count, and learning-rate setting affect reported localization losses.

fits_no_version.finding: For the lightweight KITTI regression CNN, Diag-OCP has the lowest listed validation loss at 50 and 150 iterations: 0.0139 and 0.0041. At 150 iterations Adam reaches 0.0093 and SGD 0.0151; RAdam has the lowest training loss, 0.0049, and Diag-OCP the lowest minimum validation loss, 0.0029.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects training and validation loss for lightweight visual-localization regression under limited training budgets and separately tuned learning rates.

record.code_released: Source code and results available from corresponding author upon reasonable request; no URL stated.
record.problems: One dataset and one lightweight CNN are used; the study reports localization regression loss rather than classification error or a direct train-test error gap. Optimizer parameters are tuned separately. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level held-out accuracy compared with natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance on classification or language benchmarks, including tuning, weight-decay, and optimizer-switching conditions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Comparative effects of dropout, dropout strength, dataset size, and removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized examples compared with removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All 36 numerical values match Table 2, but the rows describe optimizer-method performance outside the supplied versions. The text does not specify the training/validation split or provide uncertainty estimates. The supplied text identifies itself as a preprint submitted to Elsevier; the record's Neural Networks peer-review designation is not established by this text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label classification generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparison.
Adaptive-versus-SGD generalization on image-classification or language benchmarks; the study instead uses localization regression.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects on held-out classification error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with the training-test gap.
Removal of memorized training examples and its effect on test accuracy.
